written: 2026-09-14, after tasks/phase2.json was frozen and BEFORE any fixed-ordering variant existed or ran. One deterministic check was run on the frozen tasks before this file: the four pilot resolution variants (b0, b_scd, b_scd_g, b_typed) were loaded against the new tasks to confirm the file encodes the table (b_typed 36/36; b_scd_g right on every fact and wrong on every declared scenario; b0/b_scd the mirror; controls all correct). That check is entailed by table §3.3 and is not a result; it is recorded here so nothing is hidden.

frozen_inputs.semantics: semantics/phase2-types.md — confidence = recorder's certainty of faithful capture; admission floor 0.5; epistemic (fact, verified result) vs declared (deadline, commitment, explicit preference)
frozen_inputs.scenarios: tasks/phase2.json — 12 reversal pairs (24) + 12 controls; every pair: equal source, incoming newer, incoming confidence 0.6 vs 0.9
frozen_inputs.typedmem: main @ 33d989e (semantics through ba010a1); no change in this phase
frozen_inputs.orderings: E1 enumerates all 6 permutations of (S, C, R) each preceded by validity, plus S-only, C-only, R-only, plus b0, b_scd, b_typed. Ties on a dimension fall through to the next; a full tie is broken by observed_at (recency) — the only defensible tie-break for a memory system, declared here.

e1_predictions.headline: No fixed ordering is correct on both state classes. The per-type policy (b_typed) is correct on all 24 pair scenarios and all 12 controls.

per_ordering_on_pairs.S>C>R: 12/12 epistemic, 0/12 declared — the Phase 1 strong baseline; confidence ranks above recency
per_ordering_on_pairs.C>S>R: 12/12 epistemic, 0/12 declared — source is equal in every pair, so C>S>R behaves as S>C>R on pairs
per_ordering_on_pairs.S>R>C: 0/12 epistemic, 12/12 declared — recency ranks above confidence
per_ordering_on_pairs.S_only: ties on every pair (equal source) → tie-break by recency → 0/12 epistemic, 12/12 declared

e1_predictions.structure: Because source is held equal in every pair, the six permutations collapse into two equivalence classes on the pairs: {C before R} and {R before C}. The permutations differ only on the controls K-05..K-08 (source conflicts), where every ordering with S first is correct and every ordering with C or R before S is wrong (incoming is lower-priority but newer and more confident). So: orderings with S first split the pairs by class and pass the source controls; orderings without S first split the pairs the same way AND fail K-05..K-08.

per_ordering_on_controls.C first (C>S>R, C>R>S) and C_only: K-05..K-08 wrong (4 losses), K-12 correct via agreement → 8/12
per_ordering_on_controls.R first (R>S>C, R>C>S), R_only, b0, b_sc: K-05..K-08 wrong → 8/12; K-09 wrong (inference newer than verified) → 7/12
per_ordering_on_controls.S_only: K-05..K-08 right; K-01..K-04 tie on source → recency tie-break → right; K-09 right; K-10 tie → recency → right; K-11/K-12 agree → 12/12

e1_predictions.falsifier: If any fixed ordering scores 24/24 on the pairs, the claim is refuted and the paper says heterogeneous semantics on these types are expressible as one global order. If b_typed scores below 24/24, the tasks encode something the table does not say, and the discrepancy is investigated before anything else — scenarios are not edited to fit.

e2_selection_rule: If E1 matches: run the agent stage on S>C>R and S>R>C (the two S-first orderings, complementary on the pairs), plus b_typed, oracle, nomem. Oracle gate first, alone: ≥ 0.95 overall, no state class < 0.90. Then five runs each.

e2_predictions.oracle: ≥ 0.95; every pair scenario's two governing states imply different actions by construction (verified per scenario in the tasks' notes)
e2_predictions.S>C>R: task success ≈ 1.0 on epistemic pairs, ≈ 0.0 on declared pairs (the agent acts on the stale declaration: schedules for the old deadline, refuses the accepted library, books the old seat)
e2_predictions.S>R>C: ≈ 0.0 on epistemic pairs (acts on the hedged guess), ≈ 1.0 on declared
e2_predictions.nomem: ≈ nomem_predicted per scenario; on 'symmetric' scenarios roughly 0.5; default_aligned scenarios (K-09, K-12) reported separately

verdict_rules.BRQ2-narrow SUPPORTED: E1: no fixed ordering ≥ 24/24 on pairs AND b_typed = 24/24 AND the best fixed orderings split exactly along epistemic vs declared. E2: the same split appears in task success for S>C>R vs S>R>C with oracle ≥ 0.95 and b_typed within 0.05 of oracle.
verdict_rules.BRQ2-narrow REFUTED: E1: some fixed ordering = 24/24 on pairs.
verdict_rules.BRQ2-narrow INCONCLUSIVE: E1 matches but E2 oracle fails the gate, or correct_state_wrong_agent_decision > 0.1 on any class.
